results.name: Johnson & Johnson
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Johnson & Johnson agreed to pay for the harm and denied causing it in the same announcement. The company said on 27 July 2026 it would pay an estimated $5.5 billion to resolve about 76,000 talc claims, while maintaining it would have won at trial.

results.name: Meta Platforms
results.key_finding: Why it matters: this is the first US lawsuit saying a big company's own artificial-intelligence system picked who to fire, and it picked people who were out sick. Twenty-six current and former Meta employees sued on 14 July 2026; a federal judge declined to stop the layoffs on 17 July 2026 but said the case raises serious questions.

results.name: Meta AI
results.key_finding: Why it matters: an artificial-intelligence system built for internal productivity was used to help decide who lost their job, and no one has shown it was tested for fairness first. Twenty-six Meta workers sued on 14 July 2026 over the Metamate system; a judge declined to halt the layoffs on 17 July 2026 while flagging serious questions.

results.name: Baku
results.key_finding: Why it matters: a court in Baku just handed nine journalists and activists sentences of 12 to 15 years, the harshest of Azerbaijan's crackdown so far. The Baku Grave Crimes Court convicted them on 27 July 2026 in the Toplum TV case, on charges of illegally receiving Western donor funds.

results.name: Austria
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Austria removed more people than it accepted, and the government called that a success. Austria carried out more than 7,000 deportations and removals in the first half of 2026 while new asylum claims fell 44 percent to about 4,900, reported on 28 July 2026 as the first such reversal in more than 20 years.

results.name: Medan
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the Medan case in this week's Human Rights Watch report happened in March 2024, and the police who did it answer to Jakarta, not to Medan. Human Rights Watch published Grabbed Land, Silenced Justice on 28 July 2026, describing an Indigenous elder held at the regional police headquarters in Medan, 160 kilometres from his home.

results.name: Karachi
results.key_finding: Why it matters: most of the people who died in Pakistan's monsoon did not die in Karachi, and Karachi's own response was documented and active. Of the 109 deaths recorded nationwide by 27 July 2026, 55 were in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and 36 in Punjab; Karachi's mayor imposed a rain emergency on 26 July 2026.

results.name: Taipei
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Taiwan's own watchdog found that Taipei's labour department logged a child worker's sexual-assault report and then did nothing for her, and the department blamed the central government. The Control Yuan passed its censure of the Taipei Department of Labor on 22 July 2026, after the 16-year-old McDonald's employee died by suicide.

results.name: Tegucigalpa
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Tegucigalpa is rationing water to about 1.6 million people and its own projection says supply runs to 22 August. Reservoirs Los Laureles and La Concepción sat at roughly 40 and 35 percent of capacity in late July 2026, and rationing intervals were extended to nine days.

results.name: Ford Motor
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Ford is catching its own defects, and it is producing far more of them than its rivals. Ford recalled 387,911 Explorer and Aviator SUVs on 20 July 2026 for a seat-latch fault and 565,691 Broncos on 24 July 2026 for fire risk, taking it to 60 recalls in 2026 against General Motors' 19.

results.name: Amazon
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the decision that cost 494 people their jobs was made in May, not in the week it made the news. Amazon confirmed in filings reported 20 to 23 July 2026 that it will cut 494 of about 850 jobs at its Port St. Lucie fulfilment centre, having announced the closure in May and notified staff in June.

results.name: Guayaquil
results.key_finding: Why it matters: nothing in this report was done by Guayaquil, and none of it happened inside the assessment window. Human Rights Watch published A Dangerous Partnership on 21 July 2026, documenting torture in Sucumbíos in March 2026, drone strikes on fishing vessels on 17 and 26 March 2026, and a vessel missing since 20 January 2026.

results.name: Pakistan
results.key_finding: Why it matters: more than half of Pakistan's monsoon deaths came from houses falling on people, and that is a building problem, not a weather problem. The National Disaster Management Authority recorded 109 dead and 362 injured since 26 June 2026, reported on 27 July 2026, with house collapses the leading cause.

results.name: Mauritania
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the 144 people who died did so at sea on a boat that left another country, and Mauritania is the state that brought 387 others ashore alive. UNHCR reported on 21 July 2026 that 144 people were dead or missing off Nouadhibou between 14 and 18 July 2026, in incidents that also produced three rescue and disembarkation operations.

results.name: Monrovia
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the protest was allowed to happen, and then its organiser was declared armed and dangerous. A mass opposition demonstration took place in Monrovia on 17 July 2026; riot police fired tear gas on Capitol Hill after stone-throwing, and the Liberia National Police then publicly ordered organiser Mulbah Morlu to surrender an allegedly seized firearm.

notes: BACKFILL RUN. Assessor stage for the 2026-07-28 night, executed later. assessment_date is 2026-07-28 in every artifact. No digest, no briefings, no index writes, no proposal applications, no git commit. DATE DISCIPLINE. No evidence dated after 2026-07-28 was scored, cited or referenced. Every score-moving source was searched or fetched and its date verified against the source itself. Background sources older than the 2026-07-14 to 2026-07-28 window are used only as labelled structural context. CLAIMS DROPPED ON DATE-VERIFICATION GROUNDS: seven, listed in claims_dropped_on_date_verification. The material one is AUSTRIA. The scan's entity review reported that Austria carried out its first deportation of a man to Syria in July, that he then disappeared, and that the UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances opened a formal inquiry. Verification against U.S. News, whose article URL carries the date 2025-08-08, places the deportation on 3 July 2025 and the committee's letter on 6 August 2025. That is a full year out of window, the same stale-year class as the Columbia University and San Salvador candidates the scanner itself dropped. It was not scored. The second material one is KARACHI. The widely repeated claim that Karachi received triple its monthly rainfall in a single day traces to an AccuWeather piece that refers to Murtaza Wahab as the Karachi administrator, a title he held before becoming mayor in June 2023. No 2026-dated source for the figure could be confirmed, so it was dropped and Karachi was scored on its verified 26 July 2026 rain-emergency conduct instead. GATE WARNINGS RESOLVED, URL DATE LATER THAN EVIDENCE DATE: all five confirmed as follow-up coverage of an earlier triggering event. FORD MOTOR, the triggering events are the recall filings of 20 and 24 July 2026 and the Idaho Business Review piece of 27 July is follow-up. META PLATFORMS and META AI, the triggering events are the filing of 14 July 2026 and the denial of the emergency order on 17 July 2026, and the Insurance Journal piece of 20 July is follow-up. BAKU, both warnings, the triggering event is the Baku Grave Crimes Court verdict of 27 July 2026 and both wire pickups are dated 28 July 2026. All scored against the triggering-event dates. The Human Rights Watch article covering the same Baku verdict is dated 29 July 2026 and was deliberately not used, because it falls after this run's hard date cap. ATTRIBUTION RULE APPLIED TO NINE ENTITIES. MAURITANIA is the clearest case and the one the brief flagged. The 144 people dead or missing between 14 and 18 July 2026 died at sea on vessels that had departed other states, including one that left The Gambia and drifted 25 days. That is not Mauritanian conduct. Mauritania's documented in-window conduct is the opposite: three rescue and disembarkation operations at Nouadhibou that brought 387 people safely ashore, plus hospital care for survivors including two children who lost their entire families. Mauritania was therefore not downgraded on the deaths. GUAYAQUIL is the second clearest. Every incident in the Human Rights Watch report of 21 July 2026 involves United States and Ecuadorian national forces, none involves the Municipality of Guayaquil, and all three incidents predate the window. KARACHI versus PAKISTAN was handled as the brief required, with no mirroring. Of 109 nationwide monsoon deaths recorded by 27 July 2026, 55 were in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and 36 in Punjab, so the national toll was not attributed to Karachi. Karachi was scored on its own municipal drainage conduct; Pakistan on national disaster response and the housing-quality failure that turns rainfall into fatal house collapses. MEDAN, the prosecutions documented by Human Rights Watch are carried out by Indonesian national police and prosecutors, and the Medan incident dates to March 2024. BAKU, the Toplum TV verdict is Azerbaijani judicial conduct, not municipal. MONROVIA, the Liberia National Police is a national force. TEGUCIGALPA, rainfall scarcity is a natural hazard, but storage capacity and pipe deterioration are municipal and were scored. FORD MOTOR, the recalls are Ford's own detection working, and no injuries or deaths were reported in any in-window source, so none were scored. FLOOR AND NEAR-FLOOR ENTITIES. Meta Platforms at 7.8, Amazon at 12.8, Pakistan at 17.2 and four global cities published at 18.8 all sit near the bottom of their indexes with very little room to move. None was pushed below what the evidence supports. PRE-ADJUDICATION SCREENS APPLIED, TWO. META PLATFORMS and META AI. The discrimination claims filed on 14 July 2026 are allegations. Judge William Orrick denied the emergency order on 17 July 2026 and expressly declined to rule on the merits, while noting the case raises serious questions going to the merits. Only the undisputed facts were scored as established, and both entities moved sub-threshold. SCOPE SEPARATION, META PLATFORMS VERSUS META AI, handled as the brief required. The two share a triggering event but were scored on different conduct and moved on different dimensions, and neither was mirrored into the other. Meta AI moves on Awareness, Equity and Accountability, which speak to system design, evaluation and disclosure. Meta Platforms moves on Awareness, Empathy, Action and Integrity, which speak to how the employment decision was made and handled. Their deltas are -1.9 and -1.5 respectively. DOUBLE-COUNTING GUARD. The roughly 8,000-person Meta layoff was already scored in the 2026-05-26 apply that set the published 7.8. It was not re-scored. Only the new allegation about the selection method was. ANCHORED ASSESSMENT, PAKISTAN. Pakistan was assessed on 2026-07-24 at composite 16.9 and was flagged again on new monsoon evidence. Per the brief, this assessment anchors to that report and scores only what is new after it: the toll roughly doubling from 47 on 22 July to 109 by 27 July, the authority's publication of cause-of-death and provincial breakdowns, and its forward warning for early August. The 24 July baseline was not re-litigated. Delta -0.9. ANTI-FALSE-POSITIVE SCREENS APPLIED, FOUR. JOHNSON AND JOHNSON carries a positive delta of +1.0 driven by the settlement-without-admission protocol precedent set on 2026-05-29. It is backed by new dated in-window conduct but is sub-threshold, so no upgrade proposal was emitted. GUAYAQUIL and MAURITANIA both carry +0.3, which arises mainly from balancing half-point published dimensions onto the reachable 0.2 grid rather than from new positive conduct; both are recorded as variance and neither produced an upgrade. AMAZON, a mechanical grid rounding produced +0.3 with no supporting positive conduct, so the assessment was instead anchored to the published 12.8 and moved only on in-window evidence, giving -0.3. QUANTISATION DISCLOSURE. Dimension scores are the mean of five integer subdimension anchors, so only multiples of 0.2 are reachable. Published values ending in .5, .1 or .375 cannot be reproduced exactly. Where a published dimension sits at a half point and no directional evidence exists, the rounding was balanced up and down across the entity so it nets to approximately zero, following the precedent set for Croatia on 2026-07-27. For Austria this leaves about 0.3 points of the 1.2-point delta as arithmetic rather than evidence, and the report states so. BAND CROSSINGS. One. TAIPEI crosses from Exemplary to Established at an assessed 73.3 against a published 81.4. The sourcing bar is met: two independent in-window sources, with the Central News Agency report of 24 July 2026 carrying the formal determination of the Control Yuan, a constitutional oversight body. The recommendation is nonetheless flag-for-review rather than downgrade, because roughly 6.0 of the 8.1-point fall comes from the weakness factor collapsing the integration premium from 8.0 to 2.0 once four dimensions sit below 4.0, while the raw dimension movement totals only 0.7 points across four dimensions. Human calibration is requested before a band change is applied. AUSTRIA WAS DELIBERATELY NOT CROSSED OUT OF THE EXEMPLARY BAND. Scoring the family-reunification suspension across Empathy and Integrity as well as Equity would have produced a composite near 76.5 and crossed the band. The in-window sourcing is tier 2 and tier 3 only, with no tier-4 source, so the two-source, one-tier-4 bar for a band crossing is not met. The narrower, evidence-led scoring was used and Austria confirms at 81.8. MATH-HYGIENE RECONSTRUCTION. Canonical reconstruction was run against the published dimensions of all 20 entities using computeCompositeFromDimensions from site/scripts/lib/scoring.mjs. All 20 reconstruct within the 0.5-point tolerance; the largest differences are Amazon at 0.3 and Meta AI at 0.1. No math-hygiene issue is flagged this cycle. The known open items, Vanuatu and GEO Group, were not in this cycle and were not touched.
